context:
Goal: one uniform direction for every watch, wake, sweep, reap and log, in place of the patchwork of lessons, bugs and fixes (your note on item 180, 06:50 CST).
Problem (rule): decision the-janitor-is-one-machine-wide-sweep says the hook run cleans one repo, but the code runs the machine-wide tiers at every session end. It scans every process, and sends the report to DEVNULL, where nobody reads it.
Based on (read): the daily job already runs the machine-wide tiers.
Departs from: main — the hook run sweeps one repo; the process, sim and temp tiers run only in the daily job.

lastAnswer.note: daily job needs to have parts enter the session end too many remnant processes linger too long

options.gain: A cheap session end; the code matches its record.
options.how: The SessionEnd hook sweeps its own repo; the process, sim and temp tiers run only in the daily job.
options.label: One repo at SessionEnd; machine-wide only in the daily job
options.lose: Orphan servers and booted simulators wait for the daily job, so the simulator-boot-cap guard may refuse more often.

options.how: The record says the hook run is machine-wide.
options.label: Keep it machine-wide and fix the record
options.lose: Every session end scans every process for a report nobody reads.

ref: item 180; Sonnet workflow align-watchers (3 mappers, a synthesis and a critic), 06:58 CST
reply: Landed: claude-settings #1240 merged in batch 10 (main 59bff081, Nov 5 06:36 CST); the SessionEnd sweep is scoped to its own repository.
title: Should the SessionEnd sweep clean only the session's own repo?
why: Recommended: a. The code matches its record, and the machine-wide scan already runs daily.
